backlog.title: Distributed-PRD Include-Dedup Idempotency Bugfixes
backlog.description: Fix the two MINOR §2.3 bugs found in the distributed-PRD @token include resolver (src/core/session-utils.ts): BUG-001 (marker-mode comments contain a resolvable @token of their own, breaking idempotency when a file named like a marker word exists) and BUG-002 (the depth gate returns boundary content unscanned, leaving resolvable @tokens that re-expand on a second pass for include chains deeper than PRD_INCLUDE_MAX_DEPTH). No new features, no new dependencies; behavior change is confined to two pathological edge cases that do not affect realistic distributed PRDs. All work targets src/core/session-utils.ts + its tests + changeset-level docs.

milestones.title: Restore §2.3 Idempotency & Marker Integrity
milestones.description: Make resolvePRD a true idempotent fixed point (resolve(resolve(x)) === resolve(x)) unconditionally: marker comments become structurally non-resolvable (BUG-001) and depth-exceeded resolvable tokens are elided rather than left literal (BUG-002). Includes regression coverage and a changeset-level documentation sweep.

tasks.title: BUG-001 — Make marker comments structurally non-resolvable
tasks.description: PRD §2.3 (Issue 1 / BUG-001): the three emitted marker comments — '<!-- @include: token -->', '<!-- @end-include -->', '<!-- @include-ref: token -->' — contain a syntactically valid @token (the @ is preceded by a space so the lookbehind passes; the following word is captured). If a FILE named exactly include / end-include / include-ref exists in the entry PRD directory, the marker re-expands on a second resolution pass and breaks the idempotent fixed point. Fix: emit markers in a shape that cannot match RESOLVE_TOKEN (defeat the lookbehind OR the token-group), update the JSDoc and the byte-format test assertions, and add a collision regression test.

subtasks.title: Emit collision-proof, structurally non-resolvable include markers (TDD)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/014_347986b2effd/bugfix/001_0bc1da79f558/architecture/bug-analysis.md §BUG-001 and system_context.md. The resolver lives in src/core/session-utils.ts; worker fn expandIncludesRecursive (def ~:471) scans content with RESOLVE_TOKEN = /(?<![\w./-])@([A-Za-z0-9_./-]+)/g (:422). Three marker strings are emitted: elision reference '<!-- @include-ref: ${token} -->' (:498) and expansion wrap '<!-- @include: ${token} -->\n${replacement}\n<!-- @end-include -->' (:545). In each, the '@' is preceded by a SPACE ('<!-- @include'), so the negative lookbehind (?<![\w./-]) PASSES, and the following word (include / end-include / include-ref — all chars are in [A-Za-z0-9_./-] including the hyphen) is captured as a resolvable token. If a FILE named exactly include/end-include/include-ref (no extension) exists in the entry PRD's dir, that token stats to a file and EXPANDS on a 2nd pass, mutating bytes -> breaks the idempotent fixed point (§2.3 L27) and the 'no resolvable @token of its own' guarantee (§2.3 L26). VERIFIED: marker comments are NOT parsed/consumed anywhere in src/ (grep for end-include / include-ref / @include outside session-utils.ts returns only unrelated session/commit markers + agent-guidance prose in src/agents/prompts.ts:35) -> changing the marker byte format is SAFE; only tests assert it.
2. INPUT: the marker emission sites at src/core/session-utils.ts:498 and :545; the JSDoc blocks on expandIncludesRecursive (:429-469) and on resolvePRD's MARKERS bullet (:579-595) that describe the format; the three marker words currently emitted (include, end-include, include-ref).
3. LOGIC: Change all three marker comment strings so each is STRUCTURALLY NON-RESOLVABLE against RESOLVE_TOKEN. Pick ONE provably-correct technique and apply it consistently to all three: (A) make the char immediately BEFORE '@' a path-class char [\w./-] (letter/digit/_/./ slash / hyphen) so the negative lookbehind (?<![\w./-]) FAILS -> no match starts at that '@'; OR (B) make the char immediately AFTER '@' NOT in [A-Za-z0-9_./-] so the token group [A-Za-z0-9_./-]+ cannot start -> no match. Keep markers human-readable. PROVE non-resolvability: trace RESOLVE_TOKEN against each new marker string and confirm ZERO captures; record that trace in a comment at each emission site. TDD ORDER: FIRST write a failing regression test (markers ON; create real files named 'include', 'end-include', 'include-ref' in the PRD tmpdir; main.md includes a real file; assert resolvePRD(pass1File, {markers:true}) === out1, i.e. resolve(resolve(x))===resolve(x) byte-for-byte). Then change the three marker strings so the test passes. MOCKING: none — use a REAL mkdtempSync tmpdir like the existing prd-markers.test.ts (boundary/existence logic is only trustworthy against real files); do NOT mock node:fs.
4. OUTPUT: the three marker comment formats are collision-proof; resolvePRD(...,{markers:true}) output is an idempotent fixed point EVEN when include/end-include/include-ref files exist. JSDoc updated. Existing byte-format assertions in tests/unit/core/prd-markers.test.ts are updated to the new format: lines 61, 70, 88-92, 113-115, 235-236, plus the N2 test COMMENT at :239 (which currently — and incorrectly — claims markers 'resolve to ENOENT non-.md tokens -> silent verbatim'; reword to state the markers are now STRUCTURALLY non-resolvable). This output is consumed by P1.M1.T2.S1: the depth-gate elision emits the SAME reference-comment format, so it inherits collision-proofness.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the JSDoc on expandIncludesRecursive (src/core/session-utils.ts ~:429-469) and resolvePRD's MARKERS bullet (~:579-595) to state the marker format is STRUCTURALLY non-resolvable (cite which regex mechanism — lookbehind or token-group — defeats RESOLVE_TOKEN) and is a true fixed point even under marker-word file collisions. Update the N2 test comment at prd-markers.test.ts:239. No separate docs subtask — this rides WITH the work.

tasks.title: BUG-002 — Preserve idempotency at the PRD_INCLUDE_MAX_DEPTH boundary
tasks.description: PRD §2.3 (Issue 2 / BUG-002): the depth gate 'if (depth >= maxDepth) return content;' (src/core/session-utils.ts:479) returns the boundary file's body UNSCANNED, so resolvable @tokens in it survive literal and expand on a second resolution pass — breaking resolve(resolve(x))===resolve(x) for linear include chains deeper than PRD_INCLUDE_MAX_DEPTH (default 10; also reachable when a user lowers the limit below their actual include depth). Fix: at the gate, scan the content and elide resolvable survivors (mirroring existing cycle/diamond elision) so no resolvable token reaches a second pass; non-resolvable prose @mentions stay verbatim. Update JSDoc, update the three depth tests that assert the old literal-survivor behavior, and add deep-chain + lowered-maxDepth idempotency regression tests.

subtasks.title: Elide resolvable survivors at the depth gate so resolve(resolve(x))===resolve(x) (TDD)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/014_347986b2effd/bugfix/001_0bc1da79f558/architecture/bug-analysis.md §BUG-002 and system_context.md. expandIncludesRecursive (src/core/session-utils.ts, def ~:471) has a depth gate at :479 — 'if (depth >= maxDepth) { return content; }' — that returns the boundary file's body UNSCANNED. Resolvable @tokens (files that DO exist) in that body survive as literal survivors; on a 2nd pass they sit at depth 0 and EXPAND, so resolve(resolve(x)) !== resolve(x), violating §2.3 L27's UNCONDITIONAL idempotency MUST. Default maxDepth=10 (getPrdIncludeMaxDepth, src/config/constants.ts:1272), so it needs an 11+ deep LINEAR chain (unique files — global-flat dedup does NOT bound unique linear chains, only cycles/diamonds/back-edges) or a user-lowered PRD_INCLUDE_MAX_DEPTH (supported config §9.7.5 / hack-config.ts:403). The stale-warning code (:536-541) fires only for non-resolving .md tokens; elided/resolved tokens never warn. The existing elision path at :492-501 is the MODEL for neutralizing a resolvable token without expansion (markers off -> drop token; markers on -> emit the P1.M1.T1.S1-fixed '<!-- @include-ref: ${token} -->' comment).
2. INPUT: the depth gate at src/core/session-utils.ts:479; the existing elision branch at :492-501; the global visited Set; ResolveOpts.maxDepth (session-utils.ts ~:322); and the collision-proof marker format contract from P1.M1.T1.S1 (on which this subtask depends — it emits that exact ref-comment at the boundary).
3. LOGIC: Replace the unscanned 'return content' at the depth gate with a scan that NEUTRALIZES resolvable survivors so none reach a 2nd pass — mirroring existing elision semantics. For each @token at the boundary: stat() it; if it resolves to an existing FILE, ELIDE it (markers off -> drop the token / emit nothing; markers on -> emit the P1.M1.T1.S1 collision-proof '<!-- @include-ref: token -->' ref-comment, IDENTICAL handling to the dedup-elision branch at :492-501, so it inherits non-resolvability); if it does NOT resolve (ENOENT / directory), leave it VERBATIM (a non-resolvable prose mention re-resolves identically -> still idempotent). Do NOT recurse (that is the cap's purpose) and do NOT add boundary tokens to visited. Reuse the RESOLVE_TOKEN scan loop pattern already in the function (do NOT duplicate the regex). Preserve the stale-warning contract: elided (resolvable) tokens emit NO warning (elision = success); introduce no NEW warnings for depth-exceeded non-resolvable tokens. EDGE CASE — DECIDE + DOCUMENT: maxDepth=0 closes the gate at the entry (depth 0); under uniform elision the entry's resolvable @tokens elide (possibly -> empty output). Confirm idempotency holds (resolve of an empty/neutralized file yields itself) and document the maxDepth=0 entry behavior in JSDoc; uniform elision (entry included) is the recommended choice because it preserves the unconditional guarantee, whereas exempting the entry re-opens BUG-002 for that case. TDD ORDER: FIRST write failing regression tests — (a) a 12-deep linear chain (l{i}.md = i==12?'LEAF':`L${i} @l${i+1}.md`; main='@l1.md'), default maxDepth, assert resolve(resolve(x))===resolve(x); (b) opts.maxDepth=3 with a 5-deep chain (lowered-limit scenario), assert fixed point; (c) markers ON at the boundary emits the collision-proof ref-comment AND is a fixed point. Then implement so they pass.
4. OUTPUT: resolve(resolve(x)) === resolve(x) holds for ALL inputs regardless of include depth or maxDepth (within the cap content expands; beyond the cap resolvable tokens are ELIDED, not left literal; non-resolvable prose stays verbatim). JSDoc updated. The THREE existing depth tests in tests/unit/core/prd-resolve.test.ts are UPDATED to assert the new elided behavior (they currently assert literal-survivor): :190 'stops expanding at opts.maxDepth' (expect(out).toBe('A @b.md') -> '@b.md' elides because b.md exists -> 'A '); :208 'opts.maxDepth = 0' (expect(out).toBe('@a.md') -> elided per the documented maxDepth=0 decision, e.g. ''); :220 'default depth bound' (.toContain('@l11.md') -> .not.toContain('@l11.md'); levels 1-10 still inline; @l11.md elided). MOCKING: none — REAL mkdtempSync tmpdir like prd-resolve.test.ts; do NOT mock node:fs.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the expandIncludesRecursive JSDoc (src/core/session-utils.ts ~:454-456, the 'maxDepth is DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH only' note) and resolvePRD's MAX DEPTH bullet (~:574-575) to state the gate now ELIDES resolvable survivors (not literal) so the idempotency MUST holds UNCONDITIONALLY, and document the maxDepth=0 entry edge. Update the 3 depth-test comments in prd-resolve.test.ts (:190/:208/:220). No separate docs subtask — rides WITH the work.
